summary: A mobile-friendly web app for one neighbourhood: members list tools they lend, browse and request available tools, and the lender approves the loan and marks it returned, so everyone can see who has what.
problem: Tool requests are scattered across a chat group, nobody knows who has which tool, and lent tools go missing.
targetUsers: Neighbourhood members who lend and borrow tools
A volunteer organiser who invites members
valueProposition: Find a tool nearby in seconds and always know where lent tools are.
mvpScope: Member sign-up and sign-in with an invitation code
List a tool with a photo-free description and availability
Browse and search the neighbourhood catalogue
Lender approves or declines, and marks the tool returned
My loans: what I borrowed and lent

effort.notes: One small server-rendered web app with a SQLite database.

recurringCosts.item: Small virtual server or container host
recurringCosts.notes: Typical entry-level price; not checked for a specific provider.
Optional; a provider subdomain also works.

risks.risk: Members stop recording returns, so the loan list goes stale
risks.mitigation: Overdue loans are highlighted to both members on their loan page.

risks.risk: Personal data of neighbours is exposed
risks.mitigation: Invitation-only sign-up, minimal data, hashed passwords, sessions with secure cookies.

risks.risk: Demand beyond the chat group is unproven
risks.mitigation: Start with one neighbourhood and measure loans per week.

statements.statement: The residents' chat group gets about 10 tool requests per week.
Two drills went missing this year because loans were not tracked.
Hosting a small Node.js app with SQLite fits in the 10 USD monthly budget.
Use invitation codes instead of open sign-up to keep the community closed.

sources.title: Notes supplied with the idea
sources.notes: Chat group observations from the organiser.

openQuestions: Should members see each other's email addresses, or only names?
